svg.title: Maintenance: counter arrays, targets and list boundaries
svg.desc: First inspect thread counter shards and admission conditions. An accepted pass consumes per-list monitor hits, computes quotas and thresholds, then adjusts only overflowing LRU boundaries under the list mutex. It does not perform page I/O. Its separate direct-victim backup loops skip their bodies at the pinned revision.
svg.text: Maintenance: counter arrays, targets and list boundaries
Verified mechanism at CUBRID f799e05; schematic, not a runtime snapshot.
1. Thread counter shards
Sum sampled final unfix counts.
Time + activity admit a quota pass.
Early return does not consume a pass.
2. LRU monitor arrays
On an accepted pass, read and reset each list hit count.
Compute current rates and smoothed private activities.
adjust_age counts accepted passes, not elapsed time.
3. Quota and zone thresholds
Split the private target using smoothed activity.
Publish private quota and private/shared zone thresholds.
Targets do not reserve frames or perform page I/O.
Descriptor array traversal
Visit all private/shared descriptors.
This reads per-list numbers.
It does not inspect every BCB hit.
4. Only when adjustment is required: hold one LRU mutex
Private call gate: count_lru1 + count_lru2 > quota.
Shared call gate: protected counts > combined zone thresholds.
LRU1
warmest zone
LRU2 boundary
bottom_2 or bottom_1
LRU3
cold candidates
LRU1 may also fall directly to LRU3; page bytes stay in place.
Separate backup: VS-20 at the pinned revision
Its two list loops skip their bodies. Quota adjustment and other suppliers still exist.
Arrows show access or control flow; shared metadata still requires its own protection.
